messages:
kevin_sales: Sapphire Health wants Redwood Private in their transit VPC. Requirements: preserve original client src IP for audit, allow TLS inspection in DMZ, and a clear cost breakdown: static EIP per AZ vs shared NAT. Can we give a short checklist for their NetOps and a plain-language note for security?

mona_se: Short: Private deploy + interface endpoints is fine. Source IP preservation depends on where SNAT occurs. If traffic traverses a centralized NAT (common TGW pattern) you will see the NAT IP. Options: internal NLB with static EIP, PROXY protocol from their DMZ proxy forwarding X-Forwarded-For/PROXY header, or 1:1 SNAT/EIP per host.

raj_net: Quick topology question: are they terminating on-prem via Direct Connect->TGW or VPN into the transit? That alters guidance. TGW hairpin -> likely SNAT by NAT gateway. PrivateLink ENIs avoid that if routed directly.

kevin_sales: They plan Direct Connect into TGW. Ops still open to using PrivateLink for the service path. Security asked whether TLS inspect will break mTLS.

fei_sec: Security: TLS inspect in their DMZ is acceptable provided they retain certificate keys and we terminate mutual TLS at the connector inside their VPC. We do not support customer cert interception by us. For Private deploy we support mTLS and customer-managed KMS. I'll draft language for the security questionnaire (min TLS1.2, recommended ciphers, mTLS diagram, KMS/HSM support, audit log retention).

mona_se: Pasteable firewall snippet for NetOps (recommend FQDN allowlist if possible):

```
# Outbound egress rules
Allow TCP 443 -> *.redwood-private.<region>.svc  # service endpoints
Allow UDP 123 -> 0.0.0.0/0  # NTP
Allow TCP 443 -> <redwood-health-ips>  # optional probes

# Optional inbound for health probes
Allow TCP 443 <- <redwood-health-ips>
```

We publish IP ranges in onboarding. FQDN whitelist reduces churn.

raj_net: Practical src-IP options summarized:
- Internal NLB + static EIP on our side -> consistent external src IP, easier mapping for audits.
- DMZ proxy forwarding PROXY header / X-Forwarded-For -> preserves client IP to app if app understands header.
- 1:1 SNAT (EIP per host) -> preserves mapping but higher cost and management overhead.
If traffic passes a TGW-central NAT gateway you will see that gateway's IP unless you change path.

kevin_sales: Customer pricing ask: rough delta between per-AZ static EIP approach vs NAT gateway? Can we give a ballpark?

mona_se: Ballpark guidance: managed per-EIP sticky mapping is a Private-deploy add-on billed monthly per-EIP plus egress. Typical order-of-magnitude: tens-to-low-hundreds USD per EIP/month depending on region/contract. Shared NAT approach reduces infra cost but can't promise stable per-customer source IP on failover. I'll confirm concrete numbers with finance and update the onboarding doc.

sync-bot: [sync-bot] Onboarding checklist updated: https://redwood.internal/onboard/sapphire/connectivity (internal)

raj_net: Operational callouts: watch MTU when IPsec or encapsulation is present; recommend PMTU ~1400 for streaming to avoid fragmentation. Also suggest TCP keepalive <60s for long-lived streams and document idle timeouts for proxies. Multi-region HA: sticky egress + cross-region failover is complex; call this out as POC risk.

fei_sec: I'll add the security questionnaire answers and a short blurb about TLS inspect, mTLS termination, and KMS options.

mona_se: Action items: Mona -> one-pager decision matrix (PrivateLink vs TGW vs Peering) with src-IP tradeoffs + diagram. Raj -> DMZ proxy + PROXY protocol snippet and MTU/keepalive ops note. Fei -> security questionnaire text. Kevin -> confirm with customer if they can accept PROXY headers or want per-EIP.

kevin_sales: I'll confirm tomorrow and share the one-pager. Thanks team :thumbsup:
